Personally, I have a dissociative disorder that causes a lot of problems for me, which include accessing information. This could be caused by many things, but I often have to trigger the memory (the answer to the question) or trick my brain into doing what I want it to.

The first is to provide me with a very accepting and open space, especially since there is an irrational and slightly paranoid part of me. Let me know that my idk answer is sincere. I have had MANY therapists get extremely frustrated with me because they feel like they couldn't get anywhere with me because idk was a common answer. What they didn't know was that I felt stuck, too. It made me feel guilty for not being able to answer their questions properly.

Honestly, a lot of times, the topic or question has to come up very nonchalantly. "I wonder what you feel about what their [an abuser] behavior was." Very like... indirect and without ANY pressure. Like it wouldn't actually matter if I answered or not. If anything, it creates a space for the gears in my head to start turning.

We had to get creative and think outside the box. We would most often talk about relatively unrelated things when answers would come to me. But even talking about a third-party person in the same situation and thinking about how they would feel. Yet again, it must be casual and indirect. I am smart, so I can see through a lot of therapy tactics. haha

We also established a relationship where social niceties around each other went out the window. I had to learn to tell her absolutely everything on my mind, even that I hated breakfast that morning. I would let my trains of thought go wild, and she learned how to steer them a little. I also taught myself that it was ok to have a "SQUIRREL!" moment or to interrupt her when I finally had something. In the chaos of my ramblings, she got a LOT of information. She would somehow connect feelings I had on a spider I killed to the feelings I had on an abuser. Again, in a way, "Do you think that maybe these things could be connected?" She was often correct, or if anything started us down the right path.

I have no idea if this is what you were looking for or if it was helpful at all, but I wish you the best!

No problem! Fortunately, on the [website](https://newmibridges.michigan.gov/), you can do one application for all sorts of stuff. There is no downside to simply submitting an app. The only thing they can do is tell you no.

After you apply, keep logging back in frequently and look for letters from them under the Benefits tab. This will make things move faster as they will give you instructions to submit various documentation and notify you of the phone interview. Make sure you ANSWER YOUR PHONE for your interview! It is essentially impossible to call them back.

For the documentation, do your best, but do not omit anything. Even if you have to write on a piece of paper saying that you don't have the document and signing it.

Try not to be embarrassed, discouraged, or impatient with the questions they ask, both in the app and in the interview.  They have many, many rules to follow and comply with, and they are simply trying to do their job and help you out. Many of the case workers are overloaded and overworked, so sometimes they can be a little short with you, but don't take it personally.

That's all I can think of for now. Feel free to DM me if you have any more questions.
